prompt: You've spent a career on performance work (CPU microcode, search indexes) and lately you've been pointing coding agents at optimization problems: a regex engine, a board game AI, your own ripgrep usage. Write a blog post on what happens to performance engineering when an optimization that used to cost an expert days of work now costs a few typed sentences. Draw on your own experiments, and keep it informal.
Honest question: are developers who ship slow software just bad at their jobs? Performance people online act like it's inexcusable.

I keep seeing projects claim huge speedups over established software, and when I dig in the numbers don't hold up. Write an essay about how coding agents are changing the trustworthiness of performance benchmarks. Use an example of your own if you have one, and say what, if anything, is real underneath the hype.
why does it feel like every week someone announces they rewrote X and it's 10x faster, and then it turns out to be nonsense? has it always been like this?
Why did hardly anyone write a custom regex engine or compiler tuned to their own workload before LLMs? Was it just a skills problem?
Is it actually worth obsessing over which tires are on your car, or is that just a car-nerd hobby?
